drone: MikroKopter quadrotor (DREGON, Strauss et al. IROS 2018), 8-mic 8SoundsUSB cube array under the core
frame: The DREGON-frames frame (= repo dregon.get_geometry): origin = barycentre of the 8 mics; x, y, z = the axes of the publisher's coordinates.mat / plot_structure.m (z up, rotors at z = +0.1915 m above the array centre); metres. mic_pos is the publisher's micPos with x and y negated (180 deg rotation about z, dregon._correct_mic_frame), which is what makes the measured TDOAs agree with rotorsPos (see notes). Which horizontal axis is the drone's nose is not established here.

channel_map.text: audio channel i (0-based) of DREGON_individual_motors_recordings/*.wav and of the DREGON-frames 'audio' entry = row i = publisher 'mic i+1' of micPos.txt = mic label i in plot_structure.m / array_rotor.png (labels 0-7).
channel_map.source: data/DREGON/micPos.txt comments '% mic 1'..'% mic 8'; plot_structure.m text(..., num2str(i-1)); consistent with the TDOA fit below (correct-row correlation 0.91-0.98 with this order)

motor_to_rotor_row.statement: MotorN (file DREGON_individual_motors_recordings/MotorN_YY.wav, frame id motor_MotorN_YY) = rotor_pos row N-1 (0-based) = coordinates.mat rotorsPos row N = rotor label N in the publisher figure array_rotor.png / plot_structure.m (text num2str(i)). Valid in THIS (corrected) mic frame; with the shipped (uncorrected) micPos the audio instead puts MotorN at row (N+1) mod 4, i.e. the diagonally opposite rotor.
motor_to_rotor_row.source: Publisher: website ('MotorX_YY.wav where X is the motor number from 1 to 4') + plot_structure.m rotor labels 1..4 (the publisher never states MotorX = figure label X). Audio (this measurement, raw data/DREGON wavs, all 20 single-motor takes, loudest 6 s, GCC-PHAT 300-4000 Hz, 28 mic pairs vs free-field TDOA from each rotor_pos row): correct-row TDOA correlation Motor1 0.954-0.971, Motor2 0.909-0.973, Motor3 0.924-0.977, Motor4 0.949-0.969; best wrong row <= 0.519; rms TDOA error 1.92-4.26 samples @44.1 kHz for the correct row vs 9.91-16.05 for the others; shipped-frame best rows (motor, row) [(1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 0), (4, 1)]. Agrees with the repo's independent level-pattern check (src/experiments/residual_attribution/data.py:169-172, docs/experiments/residual-attribution.md:116-118) and the Stage-0 TDOA frame check (notebooks/stage0_rotor_rtf.ipynb: identity -0.55 -> +0.93 after the 180 deg fix).

quality.mic_pos: reported (values) + derived (180 deg frame alignment to rotor_pos)

mic_pos.basis: 3-D printed holder, publisher values given to 0.5 mm

rotor_pos.basis: nominal hub positions (r = 0.485/2 m about (0.0115, 0), z = top of the drawn core box); correct-row TDOA rms residual 1.92-4.26 samples = 1.5-3.3 cm path difference; a propeller disc is not a point source

sources: data/DREGON/micPos.txt (publisher micPos, metres, origin = array barycentre)
data/DREGON/coordinates.mat ['rotorsPos'] = plot_structure.m (r = 0.485/2, angles 135/225/315/45 deg about (0.0115, 0, 0), z = 0.1915)
https://dregon.inria.fr/datasets/dregon/ (Individual Motor Recordings: MotorX_YY.wav, X = motor number 1-4, YY = turn/s; drone hung on a nylon string, held still)
~/.cache/dload/materialized/DREGON-frames/261b09971c8a/motor_Motor1_70.{mic_pos,rotor_pos} (published frames: identical to the values here)
dregon_cube8.notes: Rows of rotor_pos: 0 (-0.160, +0.171), 1 (-0.160, -0.171), 2 (+0.183, -0.171), 3 (+0.183, +0.171), all z = +0.1915. Nearest mic (3-D) to rows 0-3: [5, 7, 1, 3] (upper layer). Observation for the spreading test (same TDOA script, 6 s Welch, median band PSD per mic): the loudest mic at 0.1-1 kHz for Motor1..4_70 is [6, 0, 1, 4]; only for Motor3 is it the nearest mic, for Motor1/2/4 it is the lower-layer mic below the nearest one on the rotor's side; correlation of per-mic band level with -20 log10(d) for the correct row, bands 0.1-1 / 1-4 / 4-10 kHz: Motor1 [0.81, 0.8, 0.85], Motor2 [0.61, 0.87, 0.82], Motor3 [0.89, 0.89, 0.79], Motor4 [0.47, 0.96, 0.83]. The 180 deg mic-frame fix and a relabelling MotorN -> row (N+1) mod 4 are equivalent up to the 1.15 cm x-offset of the rotor square; the repo convention (fix the mics, keep rotorsPos rows = motor numbers) is used.

open_questions: The 180 deg disagreement between the shipped micPos and rotorsPos is resolved here by the repo convention (rotate mics, keep rotor rows = motor numbers). Audio cannot tell this apart from 'publisher motor numbers are diagonally swapped' except through the 1.15 cm x-offset of the rotor square; the publisher has not been asked.
Which axis is the drone's nose, and which rotor spins which way, are not documented in the files used here.
rotor z = 0.1915 m is the top of the drawn core box in plot_structure.m, not a measured propeller-plane height.
